methods_quotes.q: Each case of time-loss heat illness was assigned a sample weight on the basis of the inverse of the school selection probability
These weights were summed to provide national estimates of time-loss heat illness, from which average annual estimates were calculated.
Confidence intervals were calculated by use of a direct variance estimation procedure that accounted for the sample weights and the complex sample design.
Rates per 100,000 athlete exposures were calculated based on the actual number of time-loss heat illnesses reported by the schools.
